name: logo
purpose: A third-party mark (a client, a competitor, an analyst firm, a standard or certification, a coding agent) drawn right on both themes. The asset registries already hold the files (`@aziontech/webkit/assets/client-registry`, `@aziontech/webkit/assets/competitor-registry` and the `@aziontech/webkit/assets/<file>.svg` exports); every surface that drew one repeated the same theme rule by hand (two `img` tags revealed per `[data-theme]`, a `brightness-0` silhouette, a CSS mask in `currentColor`) and none had every route. `Logo` holds the rule once: a light/dark pair of files, or one file inverted on the theme where it would vanish, or one ink (the theme's black or white, the surrounding `currentColor`, or black pinned for a coloured fill), and the company's name as a typographic wordmark when there is no file yet. It replaces the design sample's `AgentMark` and `ClientMark`. It is a renderer: it takes the file URLs from a registry entry and imports no registry itself, so a page pays only for the marks it shows.
useWhen: Use Logo for any other company's mark (client, competitor, agent, certification).
A logo wall, a trust strip, a client story card, a quote attribution, a comparison column head: any place that shows another company's mark.
The coding agents a prompt works with (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor), drawn in the ink of the surface they sit on.
A list of standards or analyst firms (SOC, PCI DSS, Gartner, Forrester).
avoidWhen: A card network beside a payment method → use `PaymentBrand`.
A person or an account → use `Avatar`.
A product icon or a UI glyph → use an icon from `@aziontech/icons`.
A grid of client marks → use `LogoWall`; it renders each mark and can render `Logo` in its `mark` slot.
related: `brand` — the Azion lockup; `Logo` is everyone else's.
`logo-wall` — the grid that lays marks out; `Logo` draws one mark.
`avatar` — a person's or an organization's picture with initials.
bestPractices: Pass a registry entry as it stands: `name`, `src` from `logo`, `src-light` from `logoLight`, `artwork` from `artwork`. The registry knows which theme each file is drawn for.

Set the height with `size`: `small` (16 px) beside a label or in a table cell, `medium` (24 px, the default) in a card or a list, `large` (32 px) in a logo wall or a quote attribution. The width follows each file's own aspect ratio. Cap wide wordmarks with `max-w-*`.
In a list of many clients, use `variant="monochrome"`: per-brand colour reads as noise next to twenty others.
On a coloured fill (white, `--primary`), use `variant="knockout"`: a fill does not follow the theme, so the ink must not either.
On a surface that is dark in both themes, or among drawn diagram parts, use `variant="current"` so the mark takes the surface's own ink.
When the text beside the mark already names the company, set `decorative`.

props.name: name
props.doc: The company or product the mark belongs to; the accessible name, and the typographic wordmark drawn when no file is set.

props.name: src
props.doc: URL of the mark; on its own it serves both themes, and with `srcLight` it is the dark-theme file. Empty draws the wordmark.

props.name: srcLight
props.doc: URL of the light-theme file; with `src` both files render and the theme reveals one.

props.name: artwork
props.doc: The ink a single file is drawn in: `light` art (for dark surfaces) is inverted on the light theme, `dark` art is inverted on the dark theme, `color` is kept as is. Ignored when `srcLight` is set or `variant` is not `color`.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Ink: `color` keeps the vendor's colours, `monochrome` paints one silhouette black on light and white on dark, `current` paints it in the surrounding text colour, `knockout` pins it black for a mark on a coloured fill.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name when it should differ from `name`.

props.name: size
props.doc: Height of the mark: `small` 16 px, `medium` 24 px, `large` 32 px; the width follows the file's aspect ratio.

props.name: decorative
props.doc: Hides the mark from assistive technology when the text beside it already names the company.
